claims.text: Microsoft’s Recall feature became a privacy scandal in 2024 because, despite claims that data would be encrypted, security researchers demonstrated that the screenshots were stored unencrypted (in plaintext) within a local SQLite database [Source: ev-1].
This made sensitive content visible on screen, such as passwords and private messages, accessible to any process running under the user account by default [Source: ev-1].
The episode was described as the first major privacy crisis of the AI PC era due to this collision between the feature's value proposition and privacy expectations for local data [Source: ev-1].
In response to the controversy, Microsoft delayed the release of Recall in June 2024 and fundamentally reversed its defaults [Source: ev-1].
The relaunched version is now opt-in (default OFF) rather than enabled by default [Source: ev-1].
Additionally, accessing the timeline now requires Windows Hello authentication and presence detection, while incognito mode and DRM content are explicitly excluded from capture [Source: ev-1].
This revised, more secure version reached general availability on Copilot+ PCs in 2025 [Source: ev-1].
